title: Vasquez: perfect = nothing lacking to true justice
source_text: XXVIII. Quod autem haec sit Doctorum Scholae Romanae sententia, dum justitiam quae regenitis inhaeret, perfectam & absolutam vocant, clarissime docet Vasquez, tom. 2. in primam secundae, disput. 202. cap. 4. num. 26. ubi haec sunt illius verba: Porro autem nostram justitiam, & sanctitatem veram esse, & perfectam manifeste patet. Nam si Scriptura docet nos justos, immaculatos, & mundos esse, ut cap. 2. memoravi-mus, efficitur justitiam nobis inhaerentem veram & perfectam esse. Dico autem per-fectam, non quod in summo, aut excellenti gradu sit, sed quod ad rationem justitiae nihil prorsus ei desit, quominus ea vere justi constituamur & simus. Et paulo post haec addit: Si ergo Scriptura absolute nos justos pronunciat, sequitur quidem tum nobis ju-stitiam inesse, tum etiam veram & perfectam esse. Idcirco perfectio nostrae justitiae non debet probari ex quibusdam Scripturae testimoniis, in quibus commendatur perfecta & insignis charitas, sed potius ex illis in quibus docemur nobis inesse justitiam: nam justitia non est quae vera & perfecta non est, eo sensu quo perfectam & justitiam hactenus explicuimus. Ubi manifestum est illum verum & perfectum pro eodem sumere, & agere de perfectione essentiae, non graduum.
pass_a_gloss: But that this is the mind of the doctors of the Roman School when they call the righteousness that inheres in the regenerate perfect and absolute, Vasquez teaches most clearly (volume 2 on the Prima Secundae, disputation 202, chapter 4, number 26), where these are his words: Further, that our righteousness and holiness is true and perfect is manifestly clear. For if Scripture teaches that we are just, unspotted, and clean, as we recalled in chapter 2, it follows that the righteousness inherent in us is true and perfect. But I say perfect, not because it is in the highest or excellent degree, but because nothing at all is lacking to it for the nature of righteousness, so that by it we are truly constituted and are just. And a little later he adds: If therefore Scripture absolutely pronounces us just, it follows both that righteousness is in us and that it is true and perfect. Therefore the perfection of our righteousness ought not to be proved from certain testimonies of Scripture in which perfect and outstanding charity is commended, but rather from those in which we are taught that righteousness is in us: for that is not righteousness which is not true and perfect, in the sense in which we have thus far explained perfect righteousness. Where it is plain that he takes true and perfect for the same, and treats of the perfection of essence, not of degrees.
pass_b_english: Vasquez: our justice is true and perfect because nothing needed for the ratio of justice is missing—not because it is at the highest degree.
He equates true with perfect as to essence, not degrees.
